sentences.text: Spectrovenator was a small theropod dinosaur measuring between 1.42 and 2.2 meters in length.
This species is notable for being the first basal abelisaurid from the Early Cretaceous known to possess a complete skull.
Remains were found in the Quiricó Formation of Minas Gerais, Brazil, located near the holotype of the sauropod Tapuiasaurus macedoi.
The genus and species were formally described by Zaher and colleagues in 2020.
The specific name ragei honors French paleontologist Jean-Claude Rage for his research on continental Mesozoic vertebrate paleobiogeography.
Researchers suggest the large openings on the skull roof likely carried blood vessels and nerves connected to the nasal and eye regions.
The authors conclude that only abelisaurids living after the Cenomanian period possessed the adaptations necessary for the group's characteristic feeding strategy.
The basal position of Spectrovenator within Abelisauridae is consistent with its age and morphology.
The animal lived at the boundary between the Barremian and Aptian stages, approximately 125 million years ago, in what is now South America.
Its time range falls within the Aptian stage, spanning from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
